anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have their primary and secondary ground pins (GND1 pin 4 and GND2 pin 5) tied to the same board-ground net USBC_D_N, even though their VCC1 and VCC2 pins are on separate nets SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V and 5V_switched_CAN.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two isolated CAN buses using isolated CAN transceivers. For ISO1050DUB/CA-IS3050G-style isolated CAN transceivers, GND1 and GND2 must remain on separate primary/secondary ground nets to preserve galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN transceivers' isolation barrier is shorted out by tying GND1 and GND2 together, so the buses are not actually isolated and can suffer ground loops or defeat the intended isolation from motor/vehicle grounds.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 and GND2 connected to the common ground net, which contradicts the specified isolated CAN architecture and defeats the transceivers' galvanic isolation.
